Q1.purpose: Monthly net revenue and orders by product
Q1.sql: SELECT o.product_id, date_format(to_date(o.date),'yyyy-MM') AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(CAST(o.unit_price_usd AS DOUBLE)*CAST(o.quantity AS DOUBLE)),2) AS revenue_usd FROM WHYDROP_FILES.orders o GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

Q2.sql: SELECT o.channel, date_format(to_date(o.date),'yyyy-MM') AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM WHYDROP_FILES.orders o GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

Q3.purpose: Refunds by month, product and reason (cross-source join: Postgres refunds x CSV orders)
Q3.sql: SELECT date_format(to_date(r.date),'yyyy-MM') AS month, o.product_id, r.reason, COUNT(*) AS refunds, ROUND(SUM(CAST(r.amount_usd AS DOUBLE)),2) AS refund_usd FROM WHYDROP_PG.refunds r JOIN WHYDROP_FILES.orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id WHERE to_date(r.date) >= '2026-08-01' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3

Q9.purpose: Refund counts and rates for P001 in August vs September
Q9.sql:
SELECT date_format(to_date(o.date), 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
       SUM(CASE WHEN r.reason IN ('changed mind','bought by mistake') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS refund_count,
       COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count,
       SUM(CASE WHEN r.reason IN ('changed mind','bought by mistake') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(o.order_id) AS refund_rate
FROM WHYDROP_PG.refunds r
JOIN WHYDROP_FILES.orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.product_id = 'P001'
  AND o.date >= '2026-08-01'
  AND o.date < '2026-10-01'
  AND r.reason IN ('changed mind','bought by mistake')
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month

Q11.purpose: Count refunds per country in the first half (1‑15 Sep) versus the second half (16‑30 Sep) of September 2026
Q11.sql:
SELECT o.country,
       SUM(CASE WHEN to_date(o.date) BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-01') AND to_date('2026-09-15') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS refunds_h1,
       SUM(CASE WHEN to_date(o.date) BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-16') AND to_date('2026-09-30') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS refunds_h2
FROM WHYDROP_PG.refunds ref
JOIN WHYDROP_FILES.orders o ON ref.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE to_date(o.date) BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-01') AND to_date('2026-09-30')
GROUP BY o.country
ORDER BY o.country

Q12.purpose: Aggregate order counts and refund counts per country for H1 and H2 September 2026 to enable refund‑rate calculation
Q12.sql:
SELECT o.country,
       SUM(CASE WHEN to_date(o.date) BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-01') AND to_date('2026-09-15') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_h1,
       SUM(CASE WHEN to_date(o.date) BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-16') AND to_date('2026-09-30') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_h2,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ref.date BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-01') AND to_date('2026-09-15') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS refunds_h1,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ref.date BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-16') AND to_date('2026-09-30') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS refunds_h2
FROM WHYDROP_PG.refunds ref
JOIN WHYDROP_FILES.orders o ON ref.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE to_date(o.date) BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-01') AND to_date('2026-09-30')
GROUP BY o.country

Q13.purpose: Compute refund rate (refunds per order) for each country in H1 and H2 September 2026
Q13.sql:
SELECT country,
       CASE WHEN orders_h1 = 0 THEN 0 ELSE refunds_h1 / orders_h1 END AS refund_rate_h1,
       CASE WHEN orders_h2 = 0 THEN 0 ELSE refunds_h2 / orders_h2 END AS refund_rate_h2
FROM (
    SELECT o.country,
           SUM(CASE WHEN to_date(o.date) BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-01') AND to_date('2026-09-15') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_h1,
           SUM(CASE WHEN to_date(o.date) BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-16') AND to_date('2026-09-30') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_h2,
           SUM(CASE WHEN ref.date BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-01') AND to_date('2026-09-15') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS refunds_h1,
           SUM(CASE WHEN ref.date BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-16') AND to_date('2026-09-30') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS refunds_h2
    FROM WHYDROP_PG.refunds ref
    JOIN WHYDROP_FILES.orders o ON ref.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE to_date(o.date) BETWEEN to_date('2026-09-01') AND to_date('2026-09-30')
    GROUP BY o.country
) t
ORDER BY country

Q20.purpose: Identify products with the largest month‑over‑month increase in duplicate purchase refunds from August to September 2026
Q20.sql:
SELECT o.product_id,
       SUM(CASE WHEN o.date >= '2026-08-01' AND o.date < '2026-09-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS aug_cnt,
       SUM(CASE WHEN o.date >= '2026-09-01' AND o.date < '2026-10-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sep_cnt,
       (SUM(CASE WHEN o.date >= '2026-09-01' AND o.date < '2026-10-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) -
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.date >= '2026-08-01' AND o.date < '2026-09-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS diff_cnt
FROM `WHYDROP_PG`.`refunds` r
JOIN `WHYDROP_FILES`.`orders` o
  ON r.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE r.reason = 'duplicate purchase'
  AND o.date >= '2026-08-01'
  AND o.date < '2026-10-01'
GROUP BY o.product_id
HAVING diff_cnt > 0
ORDER BY diff_cnt DESC
LIMIT 5

       SUM(CAST(spend_usd AS DOUBLE)) AS total_spend,

Q25.purpose: Refund rate (refunds / revenue) by product for August vs September 2026
Q25.sql:
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(TO_DATE(o.date), 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
       o.product_id,
       SUM(CAST(o.unit_price_usd AS DOUBLE) * CAST(o.quantity AS DOUBLE)) AS total_revenue,
       SUM(CAST(r.amount_usd AS DOUBLE)) AS total_refunds,
       SUM(CAST(r.amount_usd AS DOUBLE)) / SUM(CAST(o.unit_price_usd AS DOUBLE) * CAST(o.quantity AS DOUBLE)) AS refund_rate
FROM WHYDROP_FILES.orders o
LEFT JOIN WHYDROP_PG.refunds r ON r.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE DATE_FORMAT(TO_DATE(o.date), 'yyyy-MM') IN ('2026-08','2026-09')
GROUP BY month, o.product_id
HAVING total_revenue > 0
ORDER BY month, o.product_id

memory_recalled.content: [Why are refunds up in the second half of September?] REJECTED: H2 September refunds are concentrated in specific countries due to local seasonality, billing cycles, or customs issues rather than a global product problem. - H2 September refunds are driven by a global P003 "file corrupted" issue tied to the 2026-09-15 release across all countries, not by country-specific seasonality, billing, or customs.

[Why are refunds up in the second half of September?] REJECTED: Refunds are concentrated in one or two countries in H2 September due to local shipping delays, customs issues, or seasonality, not a global increase. - Refunds in September H2 are spread across multiple countries and the refund rate is uniformly 1.0, so the increase is not concentrated in one or two countries.

[Why are refunds up in the second half of September?] REJECTED: A checkout or payment duplication glitch in September caused repeat orders, driving 'duplicate purchase' refunds across products. - H7 is rejected: duplicate-purchase refunds did not rise across products in September and are not linked to repeated orders; the late-September refund spike is concentrated in P003 file-corrupted refunds after the 2026-09-15 release.

[Why are refunds up in the second half of September?] REJECTED: A surge in shipping/delivery support tickets in H2 September preceded and drove the refund increase, as customers cancelled after delays. - The September ticket data contains no shipping/delivery ticket surge split by H1/H2 (all periods are null, with only download and refund categories), and Q20 has only a without_shipping_ticket group, so there is no evidence that shipping tickets preceded or drove refunds.

[Why are refunds up in the second half of September?] REJECTED: The meta paid_social campaign sent traffic to broken landing pages in September (landing_404s jumped to 8,408), creating mismatched expectations and increasing 'not as described' / 'bought by mistake' refunds from the paid_social channel. - H3 is rejected: paid_social landing_404s did spike to 8,408 in September 2026, but paid_social refunds and the 'not as described'/'bought by mistake' counts fell to near zero, so broken landing pages did not drive those refund reasons.
